steps.text: Cook spaghetti according to package directions. Drain, rinse with cold water and drain well. Transfer to large bowl.

Whisk salad dressing, cheese, seeds, salt, paprika, garlic powder, and peppers together until well blended. Stir in cucumber and onion. Pour mixture over spaghetti and toss lightly to coat evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or up to 24 hours. Top with tomatoes to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Spaghetti Salad
raw_recipe.description: Fresh cucumbers, tomatoes, and red onions are tossed with spaghetti, Parmesan cheese, and Italian-style dressing in this easy spaghetti salad recipe.
raw_recipe.name: Easy Spaghetti Salad

review.reviewBody: In the teacher's lounge a few month's ago, a parent brought in a pasta salad from a local catering place in observance of education week (how sweet-we LOVE food)and it had a "kick" to it. This is it! Just make it with tri-colored pasta add some cubes of cheese and that one had pepperoni. Let it set for a while to blend the flavor. Instant hit! And thanks to all out there who remember us teachers!

Our favorite pasta salad. Added a chopped red pepper and a some broccoli florets. Doubled the parm in the dressing and omitted the poppy seeds. Only used half lb. of spaghetti, that was plenty. Used a whole pint of grape tomatoes, halved. We love this so much!

This is so good. I doubled the parmesan in the dressing and added a chopped red pepper and some broccoli florets. Also used a whole pint of grape tomatoes. I didn't use any of the sesame or poppy seeds. Will definitely be making this again.

Absolutely delicious! I've decided I'm having 1970's summers for the rest of my life, and this recipe makes the cut! I doubled the amount of parmesan and seasoning salt, and added black olives. Served with fried chicken and jello parfait. I will be making this salad once a week for the rest of summer...

The first time I made this it was pretty good and I made it exactly as listed. I chose it because it had a list of spices instead of the generic "italian seasoning". Before you make this make sure you like the Italian dressing you plan to use. In the future I started slightly changing things. Many other recipes add some cheddar so I did that and I added a couple more veggies. I have also tried different pastas, most work pretty good but let me advise against shells. Since most spaghetti salads are pretty similar, what I am mostly reviewing here is the spices. They work rather well. And they give you an amount of pepper instead of saying "to taste". I dislike that term especially since it is usually used in raw meat recipes.

Nice spices. Made my own dressing (recipe from this site). Halved the seasoned salt and cayenne. Didn't notice any heat so next time I will try the full amount of cayenne. Added black olives. Will double cucumbers and tomatoes next time too. My husband complained that there wasn't enough vegs. Loved the spice mix. I usually use salad supreme but this mix was great on it's own.

Great summer salad to use garden veggies. I used radiatore pasta in place of spaghetti noodles to *hold* the dressing and make it easier to pick up the pasta with a fork! Instead of bottled italian dressing I made the Italian Dressing recipe from this site and used it. Added a handful of cubed fresh mozzarella cheese. Used grape tomatoes in place of regular tomatoes. Next time I will add chopped pepperoni and broccoli and eliminate the poppy seeds.

I made this for an Italian themed potluck. Doubled everything. Used cherry tomatoes cut into quarters and added 1 red and 1 yellow pepper diced, chopped green parts of green onions instead of big onions, along with half a package of sliced pepperoni, julienned. Also added half a package of shredded parmesan cheese. It was a hit!

This is a favorite! I made it gluten free by replacing the noodles with Tinkyada Rice Pasta. I added sliced black olives, extra parmesan cheese, extra cayenne pepper, and parsley for looks. I also used white onion instead of red. Next time I would maybe use a little less Italian dressing – I like the flavor the spices naturally add versus the “store bought dressing salad”. I’ll definitely make this again.
I made this salad for a potluck and it was gone in minutes. I followed the recipe except I used a bottle of Balsamic Vinegarette.
I made this for a dinner with guests. I used Rotini pasta instead of spaghetti. I got rave reviews from our guests. My husband and I loved it too! This will be a future favorite!

Used zesty Italian, but didn’t have any of the poppy seeds or sesame seeds. Everyone enjoyed it. I know the kids don’t always like some of the other items so I left some out on the side so people could put the olives and tomatoes and cucumbers in bowls.
Was very good and easy to make! I switched the cucumbers with squash and it was fine! I will make it again!

I tweaked it a little, but everyone loved it!!
Thank you for sharing
i add cubed ham I also use creamy Italian dressing and salad supreme phenomenal
I changed it up a bit when I made this. I added less dressing and didn’t use all the recommended seasonings and it turned out fantastic!!
Family Loved it!
I didn't add paprika our cayenne pepper. Kids don't do hot stuff. But my FIL loved it so much gotta make him a bowl of his own!!
followed it to the hilt - added roasted peppers tho
I make this for summer camping trips and it is fantastic! I use zesty italian dressing.
